messages.author: ac0ecfa816a5816a
messages.subject: Issues with ODE solving.
parts:
Hi everyone,

This is my first post on the M.L. so thanks for adding me to it. I've
stumbled upon stan last week and I've been trying to use it in a project
we have in my team, whose goal is to compute the entropy of posterior
distributions to do optimal experiment design in biology. Should it be
of interest to you, our team is a joint research group between Inria and
the Institut Pasteur, and our offices are located on the latter's campus
in Paris.

The model I am currently working on is a simplistic representation of a
gene circuit known as the toggle switch. The data we have is a time
series of the behavior of the two proteins of interest of our system,
and in a first time, we want to compute the posterior distributions of
its four parameters. This requires that we solve the differential
equations of the system to get the theoretic behavior for the parameters
and then compute their likelihood. This is highly similar to the problem
presented in figure 19.4 of the reference manual.

Unfortunately, I can't figure out how to get the equation solving part
to work. As of know, shall I run the attached code on the attached data,
stan constantly fails with

100 times
> Rejecting initial value:
> Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value.

then:

> Initialization between (-2, 2) failed after 100 attempts.
> Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values,
> or reparameterizing the model.
> Initialization failed.

I've also attached the complete output.

I've tried removing part of the code to see which one has to blame and
this behavior seems to be triggered by the call to the ODE solver line
37. Note also that none of the print statements are actually outputted.

I'm using cmd-stan 2.15.0 on Archlinux.

Help on this issue would be very much welcomed, and please forgive any
error there may be in my use of this M.L. Also, feel free to ask for any
information you think might be helpful.

Best regards,
Arthur C.

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: Issues with ODE solving.
parts:
Hey Arthur

I had a look at your model. I think the issue is that the first 't' in your list of times should be greater than the initial time, t0. I made this modification to your model and it started sampling for me.

In your data you have ts[1] == 0 as well as t0 == 0. ts[1] needs to be greater than t0.

The lack of error messages is a problem some other folks have fun into recently. There's something where if an error gets thrown in initialization it's not being reported back (Stan should have been able to tell you about the t[1] > t0 thing itself). I think it's being worked on right now (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2294)

Ben

messages.author: ac0ecfa816a5816a
messages.subject: Re: Issues with ODE solving.
parts:
Hi Ben,

Thanks a lot for taking the time to look at it ! The problem you point
out is indeed what was preventing stan from going past the
initialization phase.

As for the "messages not displayed error", downgrading to 2.14 "solves"
the issue, so I think a general recommendation for mitigation could be
to use 2.14 for debugging and 2.15 for actual runs.

Arthur
